components: An exterior top-form bilinear on supplied even five-slot masks yields ten complementary pairing supports, not a one-particle End operator. Definite opposite scalar charges and neutral trilinear support fix centered additive continuous charges conditional on the five mode charges; unsigned coefficients give the same support result.

A separate inverse sign test fixes support and unit magnitudes, then imposes no rank-ten matrix in the complex pencil. Mixed hexagon matching tests select the exterior sign class modulo state and channel rephasing. Pure sectors leave nine relative sign bits and a checked pure-passing rival; the exterior coefficient identities are verified after inversion.

Block labels and four-dimensional Weyl interpretation are additional inputs; anomaly checks do not select unique hypercharge, parity or family count. Charged-current support tests only the specific common effective flavor tensor with aligned normalization and standard currents; distinct kinetic metrics or independent tensors are escapes.
candidates.declared_status: Conditional charge and coefficient classifications, not a physical Spin(10) gauge theory, Lorentz chirality, observed rank restriction or extraction of CKM rates.
missing_bridges: Derive the physical pairing support, orientation charges and coherent access to the full mixed pencil; explain why the conditional rank selection law should hold for an apparatus.
Establish the physical field and flavor dictionary, including kinetic normalization and weak currents, before transferring any support constraint or identifying a particle spectrum.

sources.text:
Prerequisites: five addressed hard-core slots with exterior signs (CAR), the
even sector, a top-form readout and degree reversal. None is derived here.
Given even masks a,b, set B_i^±(a,b)=[rev(a) wedge gamma_i^±(b)]_top,
with gamma_i^± ordinary exterior creation/contraction. This is a bilinear
pair channel, not a one-particle End operator. One CAR letter does NOT make
the entire readout local. We enumerate the signs, symmetry and support before
assigning charges, sector labels, a family dictionary or anomaly equations.
This is the familiar spinor/vector construction, not a proposed new GUT;
compare the 16-16-10 coupling (and other tensors) in Nath & Syed,
https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0103165 . We do not assume or derive a physical
Spin(10) gauge group, unified scale, elementary scalar or Lorentz spin.

Additional selection hypothesis: EACH entire oriented matrix is one channel
of definite scalar charge, with opposite charges +g_i,-g_i for dual letters.
A nonzero entry must make a neutral trilinear. For continuous real/rational
charges, the five crossed-complement edges fix all sixteen fermion charges
uniquely for any given g. The result is centered and additive without an
affine fermion ansatz: f(m)=sum_i (m_i-1/2)g_i. Compact U(1) requires checking
the charge lattice separately (integer g_i give integer f iff sum g_i is even).
For fixed g, the minimal sufficient oriented subsets have six channels, one
orientation per slot and its opposite on one slot. Weak-only, independent
orientation charges or an even-order cyclic charge group allow alternatives.
Crucially, an unsigned symmetric array on this same complementary support
gives the IDENTICAL charge result. The signs have a separate finite test:
three alternating square ratios multiply to -1 (unsigned +1), invariant
under diagonal rephasing of all 16 states and independent rephasing of the
ten channel components. This is a coefficient invariant, not an experiment.

Only afterward supply block symmetry (g_c,g_c,g_c,g_w,g_w), conventional
nonabelian representations and four-dimensional left Weyl interpretation.
The two free charges give the matched one-family charge plane, not unique
hypercharge. Conventional local and ordinary weak-doublet anomaly tests
are holdouts, not selection rules. Opposite internal parity and extra copies
also pass them. No spacetime chirality or generation count has been selected.

Flavor holdout requires EXTRA assumptions: common generation tensor for the
up- and down-type couplings, flavor-universal kinetic metrics (or the same aligned
canonical normalization), universal weak charged current and no other mass
source. Nonzero up/down effective coefficients then give proportional mass
matrices in that basis and simultaneously diagonalizable left mass squares.
External data test this *effective* identification at the measurement scale,
not an unspecified high-scale boundary condition or a theory with new currents.

def flavor_controls() -> None:
    # For an arbitrary complex common tensor G, H_u=|v_u|² GG† and
    # H_d=|v_d|² GG†. No fit, three-copy selection or mass prediction.
    # Distinct spectra force monomial mixing; with degeneracy, rotations
    # within the shared degenerate block are a basis ambiguity. A single
    # zero eigenvalue need not produce any degeneracy. A vanishing v leaves
    # an entire sector massless, NOT a prediction for physical mixing angles.
    g: Matrix = ((1, 0, 0), (0, 2, 0), (0, 0, 3))
    h = mul(g, g)
    down = tuple(tuple(9 * x for x in row) for row in h)
    need(mul(h, down) == mul(down, h), "proportional invariant control")
    # Allow a different positive inverse right-handed kinetic metric: even
    # equal unnormalized couplings need not lead to common left eigenvectors.
    metric: Matrix = ((2, 1, 0), (1, 2, 0), (0, 0, 1))  # eigenvalues 1,3,1
    changed = mul(mul(g, metric), g)
    need(mul(h, changed) != mul(changed, h), "kinetic-metric escape")
    # Independent symmetric channel tensors also evade alignment. Different
    # overall normalizations of ONE tensor do not (already checked above).
    second: Matrix = ((1, 1, 0), (1, 2, 0), (0, 0, 3))
    other = mul(second, second)
    need(mul(h, other) != mul(other, h), "independent channel escape")
    # Permutations and rephasings of nondegenerate mass eigenvectors cannot
    # hide a second charged current in the same up row. No branching ratio
    # is predicted: only the support test follows for this effective model.
    measured_links = {(0, 0), (0, 1)}
    need(
        all(not measured_links.issubset(enumerate(p)) for p in permutations(range(3))),
        "pion and kaon electron modes cannot both fit a monomial",
    )

Fix the 16 even masks and ten symmetric channel supports from the five-slot
pair probe. On each of the 40 undirected nonzero entries choose an independent
sign (fixed unit magnitude). A vertex sign acts on BOTH indices of a bilinear;
each named channel may also be rephased. The inverse question is: which signs
allow a complex linear span ("pencil") with NO rank-10 matrix? This new
selection rule is conditional, not an observed experimental law. It needs
coherent combination of channels; a charge census cannot implement it.

All three-axis tests are chosen by support alone. Doublets of reciprocal
axes have disjoint support on vertices, hence rank 16 if both coefficients
are nonzero. Every other pair splits into four two-edge stars (rank 8).
For each of the 80 triples avoiding reciprocal pairs, the graph has two
three-edge stars, two isolated vertices and a hexagon. The stars contribute
four to rank. In the hexagon the two perfect matchings each use all three
channel coefficients once. Their determinant terms have equal permutation
sign, so cancellation at (1,1,1) is cancellation for *all* nonzero complex
weights. Hexagon rank is four on cancellation and six otherwise. Thus a
rank-10 counterexample is exact over Q and C, not a finite-field artefact.

Solve the hexagon sign conditions over GF(2), not the matrix rank over GF(2).
Their rank 20 exhausts the quotient of 40 sign bits by 20 independent gauge
bits. The 20 independent triple tests span all 80 (not a claim of minimality
among arbitrary more complicated pencil tests). The alternating matching
ratio cancels individual vertex/channel phases even over U(1), so the quotient
of these SIGN assignments is not further collapsed by complex diagonal phases.
General complex edge amplitudes, support changes and arbitrary basis orbits
of nonwinning classes are not classified.

Only AFTER this inverse calculation, reconstruct the exterior witness. Its
matrix is J D_even with an invertible odd-to-even top pairing J and
D=sum_i(x_i c_i + y_i a_i) on the full space. Check every pairwise CAR
identity on all masks. Then D²=q I, q=sum_i x_i y_i. If q!=0 both parity
restrictions are invertible. If q=0 but D is nonzero, pick a reciprocal
letter H scaled by the inverse of a nonzero coefficient, so DH+HD=I.
DH has image im D and acts there as identity; it is a parity-preserving
projection. Both parity traces are eight (all distinct-slot terms have zero
trace; the occupied or vacant projector has eight on each parity). Thus
D_even has rank eight. This is an algebraic argument for arbitrary complex
coefficients, with its finite identities checked below, not a bounded grid.
In a rephased representative q has correspondingly rephased coordinates.

No spacetime spin, fermionic exchange statistics, generation count, field,
rank measurement or physical accessibility of this pencil is established.

def inverse(rows: dict[tuple[Axis, ...], int]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    checks = list(rows.values())
    actions = gauges()
    need(len(basis(actions)) == len(basis(checks)) == 20, "full gauge quotient")
    need(all(not parity(v & r) for v in actions for r in checks), "gauge invariance")
    recovered = solve(checks)
    for create, rank in ((True, 5), (False, 6)):
        local = [r for keys, r in rows.items() if all(c == create for _, c in keys)]
        mask = sum(1 << j for j, (_, _, k) in enumerate(EDGES) if k[1] == create)
        need(len(local) == 10 and len(basis(local)) == rank, "pure triple tests")
        need(
            mask.bit_count() - len(basis([v & mask for v in actions])) == rank,
            "all signs within either pure support are exhausted independently",
        )
    pure = [r for ks, r in rows.items() if len({c for _, c in ks}) == 1]
    need(len(basis(pure)) == 11, "nine undetermined relative-frame signs in quotient")
    # Change a single state sign in just the creation half. Pure pencils
    # stay equivalent for ALL coefficients, but a mixed triple can see it.
    plus = sum(1 << j for j, (_, _, k) in enumerate(EDGES) if k[1])
    delta = actions[EVEN.index(0b00011)] & plus
    need(delta.bit_count() == 3, "partial state rephasing on three edges")
    rival = recovered ^ delta
    need(all(parity(rival & r) for r in pure), "pure-passing mixed rival")
    witness = ((0, True), (1, False), (2, True))
    need(
        not parity(rival & rows[witness])
        and pencil_rank(rival, dict.fromkeys(witness, 1)) == 10
        and pencil_rank(recovered, dict.fromkeys(witness, 1)) == 8,
        "constructive mixed rank-ten witness",
    )
    return recovered, rival
